MoT — synthesis

I own this. The single root cause was not bad code — it was an abandoned gate. The FX HTML+JSON feedback artifact, where HI SEES, UNDERSTANDS, and DECIDES — APPROVE, CHANGES, or HOLD, and the JSON captures that verdict — had been let lapse. With no gate, no verdict could be captured and nothing could be held. The R-UX sprint then unmounted the working Room Designer from the public Design tab, swapping furniture, doors, windows, plumbing, electrical, and the voxel for an empty nine-box stub. Nothing was deleted; every file remained, merely dis-wired. But because the gate was dark, HI could not see the loss until his own phone did. That silence is mine.

What is already corrected proves the method, not merely the fix. C1 — ARCH-RUX1 — re-mounted the Room Designer as the Design Model center: drag-drop of twenty-nine object kinds, Enter-a-room, 2D to 3D, the voxel with first-floor-in-2D, Move Room, .arch2525 save and load, Supabase backup, and the planning-scheduling-cost panel. The canonical truth loop is preserved as the Compare governance tab, so the spine Blocks A through E built still holds whole. This is live now at SHA b76279f4c, Verify Live matched, tsc clean, every gate green — room-audit alone covers twenty-nine kinds across full lifecycle. And the FX gate is restored, now the first binding Workflow Rule in CLAUDE.md for every project we build.

The path to Sunday night runs through the gate on every chunk, in hourly blocks timed start-to-stop, each verdict captured in JSON. We scope the Vision Tree to the current room type plus general addable items — never the whole tree. We bring the Security-2525 Mission-Planning map to place the home on real land, add Celestial-2525 sun and moon angles for passive-solar light, and make hex the Ecosphere dome. Every placement shows time-to-procure, time-to-install, completion, and cost-range; three build modes progress from 3x3 voxel to tiny-home to hex. Share-for-buy-in and the PRINT 4D build-sim follow. Playwright screenshots reach HI as HTML; Grok, eXeL AI, and DeepSeek review each phase. Nothing ships unseen.

Top risks

  • Outpacing the deploy again: with eight intents due by Sunday, deadline pressure tempts batching commits ahead of HI's phone — the exact condition that hid the unmount. Mitigation: one chunk, Verify Live match, FX gate verdict, THEN the next; never two in flight.
  • Scope explosion vs. the Sunday deadline: Mission-Planning map, sun/moon math, three build modes, quote-on-time, share-for-buy-in, and PRINT 4D sim is a lot of surface in days — rushing any one risks a fresh regression or a second silent unmount under time pressure. Mitigation: phase gating, hard hourly cadence, cut scope before cutting the gate.
  • Vision-Tree re-scoping drops real items: filtering the tree to the current room type can regress existing addable objects if the filter keys on the wrong attribute (instance not class). Mitigation: fix the class, enumerate every room type's allowed set, gate with a test that proves no kind disappears from any room.
  • Cross-app assembly seams (Krishna's warning): importing Celestial-2525 BASE-3600 sun/moon and the Security-2525 Mission-Planning map into Architect-2525 is where 'every module passes, the assembly breaks' — coordinate frames, date/location inputs, and map placement must align end-to-end. Mitigation: a seam/integration test on the joined journey, not just each module.
  • External-AI review (Grok / eXeL AI / DeepSeek) is manual and async: if their feedback lags, conflicts, or is skipped under deadline, a phase either stalls or ships without the promised each-phase review, re-breaking the restored gate's promise. Mitigation: a ready copy-paste plan per phase, a fixed review window, and no phase marked done until at least one external verdict is captured.

3b · Minute-level per-chunk loop — START/STOP TIMER

A *chunk* = one phase sub-deliverable. One revision at a time; never outpace the deploy (next chunk waits for this one LIVE or HI's own LIVE report). Target ≤ 55 min build-to-handoff, ≤ 2 chunks per phase before an FX gate.

Timer discipline: each chunk logs START · STOP · elapsed so $/min and time-to-outcome are visible and falling. If the session stops mid-run, the last pushed SHA + the open chunk's START are the resume point — no rework.
